newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini to meet Milosevic on Yugoslav crisis.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini to meet Milosevic on Yugoslav crisis.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini is to visit Belgrade on Thursday for talks with Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and opposition leaders.
The visit, which Dini confirmed on Wednesday, follows 24 days of street protests in the Yugoslav capital after the annulment of opposition local election victories by Milosevic's ruling socialists.
"I am going to Belgrade to assess the situation in the hope that I can make a contribution to resolving the crisis under way," Dini told reporters in Milan.
Diplomatic sources said the mission had the backing of NATO and that the United States had been informed.
Dini would also meet Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic and planned to talk with leaders of the Zajedno (Together) coalition of opposition parties, the sources said.

The West has supported demonstrations by up to 150,000 students and opposition supporters a day in Belgrade, which were joined for the first time on Wednesday by workers from independent trades unions.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher warned Milosevic on Wednesday that continuing his "repressive, undemocratic stance" would doom his dreams of ties to the West.
Dini is a member of the European Union's "troika" of foreign ministers from the past, present and future holders of the EU's rotating presidency.
